electrical.electrical_power.title: Electrical power and energy (P = V·I, E = P·t)
assumptions: DC or unity-power-factor AC (for reactive loads use the AC power calculator).
method_references: P = V I; E = P t

electrical.resistance_series_parallel.title: Series and parallel resistance (two resistors)
assumptions: Two resistors; for more, chain the rule (1/Rp = Σ 1/Ri).

electrical.capacitance_series_parallel.title: Series and parallel capacitance (two capacitors)
assumptions: Two capacitors; note capacitance adds in parallel, the opposite of resistance.

electrical.inductance_series_parallel.title: Series and parallel inductance (two inductors, no coupling)
assumptions: Magnetically uncoupled inductors; mutual inductance changes both combinations.

electrical.rc_transient.title: RC time constant and charging voltage
assumptions: Series RC, capacitor charging from 0 toward V0 after a step; reaches ≈63% at t = τ and ≈95% at t = 3τ. Discharge replaces (1 − e) with e. Solving for t with Vc ≥ V0 has no finite solution (t → ∞) and raises an error.
method_references: τ = RC; t = −τ ln(1 − Vc/V0) (charging from 0)

electrical.rl_transient.title: RL time constant and current rise
assumptions: Series RL energised by a step; current rises toward V0/R with the same 63%/95% milestones. Interruption causes an inductive kick — use a freewheel diode.

electrical.dc_motor.title: DC motor: torque, back EMF, speed, no-load and stall points

variables.name: E
variables.desc: back EMF at the operating speed

procedure.python:
def _dc_motor(v):
    """Steady-state permanent-magnet / separately-excited DC model: V = I·R + ke·ω, T = kt·I.

    Adds the back EMF E = ke·ω, the no-load speed ω_nl = V/ke (T = 0) and the stall torque
    T_stall = kt·V/R (ω = 0). T above the stall torque would need ω < 0 and raises MechError; a
    mismatch between kt and ke is surfaced as a warning (they are equal in coherent SI for an ideal
    machine).
    """
    V, R, ke, kt, T = v['V'], v['R'], v['ke'], v['kt'], v['T']
    if R <= 0 or ke <= 0 or kt <= 0:
        raise MechError('R, ke and kt must be positive')
    T_stall = kt * V / R
    if T > T_stall:
        raise MechError(f'T = {T:g} N·m exceeds the stall torque kt·V/R = {T_stall:g} N·m at this supply '
                        f'voltage — the motor cannot develop this torque (it would need ω < 0)')
    I = T / kt
    omega = (V - I * R) / ke
    E = ke * omega
    P_out = T * omega
    P_in = V * I
    eta = (P_out / P_in) if P_in != 0.0 else 0.0  # efficiency → 0 as the load vanishes
    omega_nl = V / ke
    warnings = []
    if abs(kt - ke) > 1e-12 * max(1.0, abs(ke)):
        warnings.append(f'kt = {kt:g} N·m/A and ke = {ke:g} V·s/rad differ; in coherent SI units they are '
                        f'equal for an ideal lossless machine — check the units or gearing')
    return {'omega': omega, 'I': I, 'E': E, 'P_out': P_out, 'P_in': P_in, 'eta': eta,
            'omega_nl': omega_nl, 'T_stall': T_stall, '_warnings': warnings}

assumptions: Steady-state permanent-magnet / separately-excited model; brush and iron losses neglected except as captured by the efficiency. In coherent SI units kt = ke for an ideal machine (kt in N·m/A equals ke in V·s/rad); a warning is raised when they differ. A load torque above the stall torque kt·V/R (which would need ω < 0) raises an error.
method_references: DC motor equivalent circuit V = I R + ke·ω; T = kt·I; η = Tω/(V I); stall torque kt·V/R; no-load speed V/ke

electrical.ac_power.title: AC power: apparent, real, reactive and power factor

variables.name: phi
variables.desc: phase angle of current relative to voltage (negative = leading)
variables.label: φ

assumptions: Sinusoidal single-phase AC; S, P, Q are dimensionally watts but reported as VA, W, var. φ > 0 is a lagging (inductive) load, φ < 0 leading (capacitive). pf = cos φ ignores harmonic distortion.
method_references: S = V I; P = V I cos φ; Q = V I sin φ; pf = cos φ

electrical.stepper_motor.title: Stepper motor step angle and resolution
assumptions: Variable-reluctance stepper relation θ = 2π/(m·Z_r): a 4-phase motor with 50 rotor teeth steps 1.8° (200 steps/rev). A hybrid stepper with a two-pole rotor halves this (θ = 2π/(2·m·Z_r)) — enter the equivalent Z_r. Microstepping divides each full step by μ, raising resolution but not guaranteed positional accuracy.
method_references: Step angle = 2π/(m·Z_r) from the number of phases and rotor teeth; resolution = m·Z_r·μ steps/rev

electrical.gearmotor_output.title: Gear-motor output torque and speed (gearbox with efficiency)
assumptions: Single-stage equivalent; efficiency multiplies torque, not speed. Ideal (η = 1) speed/torque ratio alone is gears.gear_ratio.
method_references: ω_out = ω_in/i; T_out = i·η·T_in; power conservation with loss

electrical.encoder_resolution.title: Encoder resolution (counts and angle per count)
assumptions: Quadrature encoders decode both edges of both channels, so ×4 gives 4 counts per line. m = 1 (×1) or 2 (×2) if only one channel/edge is used; other multipliers are rejected.

electrical.pwm_duty_cycle.title: PWM duty cycle, frequency and average voltage
assumptions: Averaging model: the load (e.g. a DC motor) responds to V_avg when the switching frequency is far above the load time constant; current ripple is neglected.
